claims.text: Current high-entropy-alloy intermediate layers typically have equiaxed, isotropic microstructures.
Rapid directional solidification followed by thermomechanical treatment will produce vertically aligned columnar grains in AlCoCrFeNi-based intermediate layers.
The proposed columnar grains will form continuous thermal pathways along the thermal gradient.
Directional solidification forces grains to align with the heat-flow direction.
Alignment of columnar grains with the heat-flow direction reduces thermal resistance along that direction.
Transverse grain-boundary constraints in the columnar architecture preserve or enhance structural stability.
The intervention will significantly increase directional thermal conductivity relative to current intermediate-layer performance.
The treated alloy will retain mechanical strength similar to that of the conventionally processed control.
The treated alloy will retain ductility similar to that of the conventionally processed control.
High surface temperature, rapid thermal cycling, high thermal gradients, mechanical stress, and irradiation are representative plasma-facing reactor conditions.
The proposed benefits should persist at temperatures of at least 700 degrees Celsius under rapid thermal cycling and high mechanical loads.
The intervention should not compromise long-term structural integrity under severe plasma-facing conditions.
Laser-flash analysis can measure directional thermal conductivity for comparison of the treated and control samples.
SEM and EBSD can determine whether the treatment produced a consistent vertically aligned columnar grain structure.
The exact magnitude of the heat-transfer improvement and the long-term behavior under irradiation are uncertain.
Potential mechanical-anisotropy tradeoffs require further investigation.
